subject: Reasoning
topic: Letter Series and Alphanumeric Patterns (W12 B1)

questions.stem: What is the next term in the series: B, D, F, H, J, ?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Rule: every alternate letter (skip one between each). B(2)→D(4)→F(6)→H(8)→J(10)→L(12). Each letter advances by +2 positions. Verify: B+2=D, D+2=F, F+2=H, H+2=J, J+2=L ✓. These are consecutive even-positioned letters. Trap: K(11) = +1 from J (wrong skip); M(13) = +3 from J (wrong).

questions.stem: What is the next term in the series: Z, X, V, T, R, ?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Rule: descending, skipping one letter (−2 each step). Z(26)→X(24)→V(22)→T(20)→R(18)→P(16). Verify: Z−2=X, X−2=V, V−2=T, T−2=R, R−2=P ✓. These are consonants in reverse order (skipping vowels: Y, W, U, S, Q are the skipped letters). Trap: Q(17) = just one below R (−1 not −2); N(14) = −4 from R (wrong).

questions.stem: What is the next term: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Differences in position values: A=1, C=3 (+2), F=6 (+3), J=10 (+4), O=15 (+5). Next: +6 → position 21 = U. Pattern: gaps increase by 1 each time (+2,+3,+4,+5,+6...). Verify: A(1)+2=C(3)+3=F(6)+4=J(10)+5=O(15)+6=U(21) ✓. Trap: T(20) = only +5 from O (same gap as previous, not increasing); S(19) = wrong.

questions.stem: What is the next term: AB, CD, EF, GH, ?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Rule: consecutive pairs of letters. AB (1,2), CD (3,4), EF (5,6), GH (7,8), IJ (9,10). Each pair is the next two consecutive letters in the alphabet. Verify: after GH (7,8), next pair = IJ (9,10) ✓. Trap: HI = starts at H (8), overlaps with previous pair; KL = skips IJ entirely.

questions.stem: What is the next term in the alphanumeric series: A2, C4, E6, G8, ?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Letter pattern: A, C, E, G, I (every alternate letter, +2 each: vowels A, E and consonants C, G, I alternating). The next letter after G = I (G+2=I). Number pattern: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 (even numbers increasing by 2). Next number = 10. Combined: I10. Verify: G+2=I ✓; 8+2=10 ✓. Trap: J10 = J is not alternate from G (G(7)+2=I(9), not J(10)); I9 = number should be 10 not 9.

questions.stem: What is the next term: AZ, BY, CX, DW, ?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Pattern: First letter advances from front (A,B,C,D,E); second letter retreats from back (Z,Y,X,W,V). Together each pair uses positions (1,26), (2,25), (3,24), (4,23), (5,22) = positions summing to 27. Next pair: E(5)V(22) → sum=27 ✓. Verify: A+Z=1+26=27; B+Y=2+25=27; C+X=3+24=27; D+W=4+23=27; E+V=5+22=27 ✓. Trap: EU = V=22, U=21 (one short); FV = F is 6th, not 5th (wrong front letter).

questions.stem: Find the odd one out in the letter group: QRS, BCD, MNO, GHJ
questions.explanation: D is correct. QRS: Q(17),R(18),S(19) — consecutive ✓. BCD: B(2),C(3),D(4) — consecutive ✓. MNO: M(13),N(14),O(15) — consecutive ✓. GHJ: G(7),H(8),J(10) — NOT consecutive (skips I=9). The odd one out = GHJ (should be GHI for consecutive). Trap: all four groups appear similar; careful position-checking of GHJ reveals the skip from H(8) to J(10).

questions.stem: What is the next term: Z1A, Y2B, X3C, W4D, ?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Three patterns simultaneously: First letter (descending from end): Z,Y,X,W,V. Middle number (ascending): 1,2,3,4,5. Last letter (ascending from start): A,B,C,D,E. Next: V(letter from end), 5(number), E(letter from start) = V5E. Verify: Z(26)→Y(25)→X(24)→W(23)→V(22) ✓; 1→2→3→4→5 ✓; A(1)→B(2)→C(3)→D(4)→E(5) ✓. Trap: U5E = uses U instead of V (goes too far back); V5D = D already used (should be E).

questions.stem: If A=1, B=2, C=3... Z=26, what is the value of EXAM + PASS?
In a code where each letter is replaced by the letter that is 3 positions after it in the alphabet (Z wraps to C, Y wraps to B, X wraps to A), what does 'KHOOR' decode to?
questions.explanation: A is correct. Each letter in the code is 3 positions AFTER the original. To decode, shift BACK 3 positions (−3). K(11)−3=H(8); H(8)−3=E(5); O(15)−3=L(12); O(15)−3=L(12); R(18)−3=O(15). Decodes to: HELLO. This is the classic Caesar cipher with shift 3 (as used by Julius Caesar). Verify: H→K (+3) ✓; E→H (+3) ✓; L→O (+3) ✓; L→O (+3) ✓; O→R (+3) ✓. Trap: JELLO = shifts back only 1 (J=K−1 not K−3); WORLD = a different famous word but doesn't decode from KHOOR.
